quest.title: An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade
quest.description: Help the Adeptus Fujin complete a ritual that will heal the land of Chenyu Vale.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Primogem x50, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! Mao, look out behind you!

choices.text: Whoa, that's a huge monster!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Huh? Oh, no, no, she's my friend! Didn't I tell you before that I had a lot of friends? I just happened to meet her, so I "got a hold of her" to introduce to you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, well, hello?

choices.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}, and this is Paimon.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Um... She's... afraid of strangers. I usually call her Bluey, because I don't really know her name.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: #Oh, don't you worry about that. {NICKNAME} and Paimon are great people. They've been accompanying me on my adventures! They're real experts in mountains and forests, too!

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I know. I've seen. Answer me this one thing. Where did you gain the power to suppress nature?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Suppress nature... What do you mean?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Plants pursue the sunlight and fertile soil, creating fruit fit for the birds and beasts to consume. The digested seeds are scattered, and those which consume seed and fruit become bait for predators. Thus does everything return to the land.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: The snake hidden in the branches, the fish in the mountains, and the beasts of the forest. Traveling in the realm of nature is wonderful, so why have you come?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Oh, come on, Bluey, you don't have to be so fierce...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...You raised two questions.

choices.text: My "adeptal energy" comes from Adeptus Fujin.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And we need to help her rejuvenate the water and soil of Chenyu Vale.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly. Something's off about Chenyu Vale's natural conditions, so Adeptus Fujin's enlisted our help! If we don't... Well, the tea leaves in Qiaoying Village are gonna turn out worse and worse, and the village itself might decline!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's why she wanted us to perform the Rainjade Rite, which will restore the area!

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: The Rainjade Rite. I see. You have answered two of my questions. You may ask me two also.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why do we have to do that?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Give and take. It is only natural. You have one more question.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Wait! That one counted? Ugh, whatever. You ask, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: Little Mao said that you want to "restore nature"...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is that the same as "nursing the water and soil"?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: ...Not the same.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Eh? It isn't? {NICKNAME}, what were you talking about?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: That's right, what do you mean "not the same"?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: ...The new tea leaves taste better. More like before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? More like... Whoa, and just like that, she's gone!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Don't worry about it, Paimon, she's like that! Sometimes, when I'm not looking, she'll just vanish into the shadow of the trees. Then at others, the sun might dazzle me, or the birds might call overhead... and there she is.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: In any case, guess we're all friends now!

choices.text: Nice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, your friend's pretty strange, Little Mao.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Is she? Well, for all you know, you're the one who might seem strange to others.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: I mean, not only can you use adeptal energy to make the moss disappear, but you can make the golden stone things appear and vanish, and even turn into a Carp and fly around, like in the stories!

choices.text: #After all, I'm none other than the {M#Young Master}{F#Young Lady} of the Feiyun Commerce Guild.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wha...?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, Paimon couldn't have imagined that the "friend" you always spoke about was ... Well, "monster" seems a bit rude, and "thing" might be pretty offensive... That's right, your friend's so blue! No wonder you call her Bluey!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe. That's why I've never told anyone. If the adults knew that we were friends, they might lock me up!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, really!? You'd go to actual prison?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: No, no, not like that! They just wouldn't let me go out, make me wash my face, and force me to read my books... I wouldn't get to play in the mountains anymore.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe. And that's why I've never told anyone. But you're my friends, so it's fine! Anyway, come with me!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: There's an awesome place I'd love to show you!

choices.text: You've got a point.
Let's hope so.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: #Um, just don't worry about it, {NICKNAME}. Bluey's not big on politeness, but she's always been like that!

choices.text: Do you know Adeptus Fujin?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Yes, I do know Fujin.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Basically, Adeptus Fujin has asked us to help nurse the soil and water in Chenyu Vale, so that the tea leaves in Qiaoying Village will recover their original flavor!

choices.text: Our goal is to nurse the soil and water in Chenyu Vale.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And the "adeptal energy" we use comes from Adeptus Fujin.

choices.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}, and this is Mini Pie.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What kinda name is that!? Paimon's Paimon!

choices.text: We're friends of Little Mao's.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{M#He}{F#She}'s {NICKNAME}, and Paimon's name's Paimon!

choices.text: Get behind me. I'll settle this.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Huh? Oh, no, no, she's my friend! Didn't I tell you before that I had a lot of friends? I just happened to meet her, so I "got a hold of her" to introduce to you!

choices.text: Wait, your friend, you say?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: That's right! I told you before that I had a lot of friends, didn't I? Well, I just happened to meet her, so I "got a hold of her" to introduce to you!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: I wonder where she's off adventuring nowadays. I can't wait to receive my next letter from her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, this Big Sis of yours sure seems like an interesting person!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: I know, right? Still, Big Sis Fujin needs our help, so let's continue on!

dialogues.speaker: Fujin's Voice
dialogues.text: Oh, there you all were. Ah, I was so worried...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, a Golden Carp!

dialogues.speaker: Fujin's Voice
dialogues.text: ... *cough* One was quite concerned that the swirling miasmas and fierce beasts that roam might have caused you ill. But one sees that it is not so, and that is good.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin's Voice
dialogues.text: #Thanks to the adeptal energy you possess, {NICKNAME}, one has been connected to the Golden Carp here, thus gaining the means to speak with you directly.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin's Voice
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, Little Mao, please come with me.

talks.objective: Take care of the nearby miasma

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: However, she hasn't written to me in a long time. If I were to guess, she's off adventuring in some faraway place. Maybe in the "Ancient City of Ys," or something like that.

choices.text: Yeah, that sounds about right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh, this Big Sis of yours sure seems like an interesting person!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: I know, right? Still, Big Sis Fujin needs our help, so let's continue on!

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: Oh, there you all were. Ah, I was so worried...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, a Golden Carp!

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: ... *cough* One was quite concerned that the swirling miasmas and fierce beasts that roam might have caused you ill. But one sees that it is not so, and that is good.

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: #Thanks to the adeptal energy you possess, {NICKNAME}, one has been connected to the Golden Carp here, thus gaining the means to speak with you directly.

response.speaker: Fujin's Voice
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, Little Mao, please come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Much time has passed since I last emerged here.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: This was once a lively place, filled with the aroma of incense... Then, the three of us could travel freely across the mountains and rivers.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Yes... Those days were like flowing water 'neath the moon, dark, yet sparkling oh so brightly...

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Ah, but enough reminiscing.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Thanks to you all, I am now able to return here and host the Rainjade Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? So... you're that person in the mural?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Oh, I get it now! That person... standing on the mountain, hugging that egg, that was you, wasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Ah— An egg? Come now, Little Mao, that was precious jade!

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: "Casting Rainjade" is a ritual of great power. The Votive Rainjade can calm rivers, improve the weather... But it can also be a thing of death and slaughter. Only the thinnest line separates curses and the adeptal energies that have aided you up till now.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: That is why I must make sure that the Rite does not fall into the hands of those who would do ill. That's why... Ahem, yes, that is correct, one was indeed the figure who "hugged that egg" in that mural.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Huh... Big Sis Fujin, doesn't this make you pretty, uh, ancient?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Yes, it does. Still, I do like the name "Big Sis." It does quite make me feel young!

choices.text: Well, being called "adeptus" is pretty alright too.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Well, certainly! Though even if others title me as such, I am aware that I am hardly the equal of true adepti like Mountain Shaper and the rest.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: I am, in truth, the weakest of my band of friends. I cannot make medicines to save others, nor can I bound across the mountains and plains. Even so, I could not simply lay the title down.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: It would have done the people of Chenyu Vale a disservice, I fear.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Still, you may call me whatever you wish. After all, we... have become friends, or so I would say.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: In any case, my days of being called an adeptus are now consigned to history, just like this place has been.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Once, the Rainjade Rite was a day of great celebration, where we would commemorate the year of abundance, using laughter, firecracker battles, and beast dances to frighten the ill omens away. This must appear like naught but forgotten ruins to the modern mind.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, not completely forgotten...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. People in Qiaoying Village told us that it was the mighty Adeptus Fujin who defeated the demons and planted the first tea tree. Back on the bamboo raft, Grandpa Lu also mentioned that the offerings of tea were to a certain Carp adeptus.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: And wasn't there that opera sung at Yilong Wharf about the Carp going around killing stuff? Hehe, you were so awesome in those stories, Big Sis Fujin! Also, people still do the Wushou dance, you know!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You said it yourself. The definition of an "adeptus" is...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, putting definitions aside, you're our friend, Fujin! You shouldn't be constantly fretting about the rite and stuff. You should live happily — like we're companions on an adventure!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: That's right, we're on an adventure together!

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Right... Yes, you're right! Thank you — that was well said! Indeed. I was the one who asked you all for help. It wouldn't do at all if I just continued wallowing in the past, now would it?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: In any case, I'll need your help to prepare for the Rite itself.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: In any case, have you encountered any Sacred Simulacra in your adventures? Those were ritual spirits often used by people in ancient times to protect their homes. There should be some nearby.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, Little Mao, please help me put the Simulacra in their proper places. That way, we can restore the spirit veins using the Rainjade Rite.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Leave it to us.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: I will. I have faith in you.

choices.text: Well, being called "adeptus" is pretty alright too... right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Sacred Simulacra are all ready!

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Thank you both. The Votive Rainjade has been returned to its priests, and the statues have come back to their rightful places. The Rainjade Rite is now ready to be performed.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: ...But will Chenyu Vale really recover once you cast the Rainjade in?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: That's right. Things will get better for us, Little Mao. Nature, jade, humans... All is divinely dictated. The changes in the land and water in Chenyu Vale, the malicious fog in the spirit veins... They are all essentially a sign of the earth moving against the flow of time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. Huh, so that miasma-like thing is a manifestation of environmental disorder...?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's right. You can think of it like Chenyu Vale's attempt to... How to put it? Return to nature? And what we intend to do here is to treat the land and soil, and rid it of this sickness.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Return to nature"?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: After all, before humans left their caves and mountains to dominate the world and regulate nature, and before Chenyu Vale or Bishui River got those names, the land, mountains, and rivers had their own order.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Hehe, even I sometimes miss the cool mountain streams, and the great rivers that would ebb and flow with the seasons. I mean, I was once a mere fish that swam...

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: But if we let nature seize control of its order once more, the people of Chenyu Vale will suffer and languish. I hope you can understand.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Yeah...

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: In that case...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Did it work?

choices.text: That thing in the fog just now...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: It seems I am too feeble in my current state.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? We got the Votive Rainjade, and we placed the Simulacra, but it still wasn't enough?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: I'm very sorry — it is not your fault. I need more power to overcome this trial. Just as the adeptal energy in the Votive Rainjade has dissipated into the spirit veins, so has my power also left me across the long years.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Huh? Will you grow really big just like the jade?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: P—Probably not...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, just think about it, though — Super Adeptus Fujin, now three times the size! Well, is there any way we can restore your power?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Golden Carp.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}, you are wise indeed. Before you found a few Golden Carp, I could not even muster the strength to appear. Initially, I thought that we just needed to gather all the ritual implements, and that would make up for the deficiency in my power...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...I was not entirely open with you before, but neither the present nor past me was anywhere near a match for the adepti of the south. I... feared you would consider me weak and unworthy of your help...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Gee, is that it? Paimon thought you'd have something more important to say!

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Eh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no way we'd abandon or not make friends with you just because of that!

choices.text: #That I, the {M#Young Master}{F#Young Lady}, consider you a friend is not conditional on your status as an adeptus.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Other than that whole "{M#Young Master}{F#Young Lady}" bit, Paimon wanted to say the same thing!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: My friend told me lots of stories about you. In my mind, even though we've just met, we're already friends, and I also want you to be happy, Big Sis!

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Alright, alright... Thank you, all of you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's more like it! So, where should we start looking for these Golden Carp?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: I believe that you will have to go to Yaodie Valley. There will be a cavern there with a Golden Carp hidden within.

choices.text: That you are my friend has nothing to do with your status as an adeptus.
Nothing seems to have changed...

talks.objective: Take care of the nearby miasma

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: We're here, Big Sis Fujin! Have you been waiting for us here all this time?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: #Hehe, no, no. After leaving Carp's Rest, I can only appear in places in which my power remains, and only by the grace of your adeptal energy, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute... Didn't the gap in the middle of that mural originally have something that went with the Golden Carp mural in it?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: ...I'm not sure. In truth, this is my first time seeing this mural as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: I'm sure you've all heard of the battles that took place in the past.

choices.text: Khaenri'ah...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Hmm?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Sorry, I am merely a minor adeptus of Chenyu Vale. I fear I know little about any wars concerning this "Khaenri'ah."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Archon War?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Yes. This cave was one of the shelters we built for the inhabitants of Chenyu Vale, such that the innocents caught in the crossfire when the floods overturned the heavens and the earth split open could have a place of safety.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: I didn't expect that they'd draw a mural here, though. I believe the ones depicted to be me... *cough* I mean, the "big, slippery Carp" Little Mao mentioned, and a friend.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Huh... If that's the case, why did the most important part get taken somewhere else?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: That's true. Why is that?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...Perhaps dissatisfaction. The three of us were once great friends, with two of us becoming worshipped as adepti, and one of us was always the mountain's master.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Later, Herblord and I defected together, and she most likely died too. Or perhaps, the one amongst us who fought to the last never submitted, and only heard news of us afterward.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Perhaps, to her, we were all traitors, with the depictions of myself and Herblord becoming an object for her to vent her fury against.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Huh... Is that really the case? The painting outside looks like...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Who knows? In any case, that's all in the past.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: So please, lend me your strength in nursing Chenyu Vale back to health. I can feel that there's another Golden Carp lingering where I used to... Near Mt. Xuanlian, I believe.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh, so there's another?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: If we get that one, I should have enough strength to perform the ritual.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Speaking of that, I must apologize for being unable to control the Golden Carp even with you nearby. I know they might have given you some trouble, swimming through the air like that.

choices.text: That was somewhat troublesome, yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But really, where is the Golden Carp that should be here?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #Hehe, well, inside the painting. Just use your adeptal energy to awaken it, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: It's fine, I just think of them like Seelie.
The Archon War...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, there's a pavilion here on this mountain!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's rather adepti-style.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Paimon wonders where we'll find that Golden Carp. This place is kinda huge!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: #Maybe we can do what we did last time? You know, {NICKNAME}, the bit where you used adeptal energy on the mural, and the Carp turned out to be hiding inside?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: #Look, {NICKNAME}! There's four stone Carp statues here! Do you think there might be four giant Carps hiding inside?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh. That does make sense. You're pretty smart, Little Mao! {NICKNAME}, is the adeptal energy reacting in any way?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not at all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...But there seems to be something missing inside.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... That might be where the critical clue lies.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}, over here! It looks like there's an orb inside some of these Carp statues!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Didn't we find some statues of Carps and large pearl on our way down the mountain? Maybe those are actually used for something!

choices.text: A real pearl of wisdom.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, let's give it a go, then!

choices.text: That's worth a try. Good job, Little Mao.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe...

talks.objective: Use your adeptal energy to activate the Spirit Orb

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: My apologies for the poor hospitality. It has been a long time since I last enjoyed tea with others. Hopefully, my brewing skills have not deteriorated too much over time.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: One d— *ahem* I mean, I have some experience in appreciating tea. It was also thanks to this that I was able to tell that this year's tea offering smelled off. That was how I discovered the trouble with the soil and water quality.

choices.text: Huh. Didn't think the offering rites would be so useful.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #Hehe, I suppose now I can tell those who fail to appreciate the value of tea about its value with confidence. Come, {NICKNAME}, have some tea!

choices.text: Is this your teapot, Fujin?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, there was that time in Liyue Harbor when we fixed Madame Ping's teapot for her! Hehe, if you think about it, we seem to have quite a connection with tea!

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Madame Ping? ...Ah, I think I know of whom you speak. We were acquainted back in the day, along with her friends.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: As Little Mao said, I was once just a "giant Carp," unable to leave fresh water for too long, nor live in salty waters. As such, they sent me one of these "teapots."

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: That was how my friends would have been able to take me — inside my teapot, of course — to Guili Plains and Liyue Harbor, to meet those lovely people they spoke of. Unfortunately, such a time never quite came.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you've been to Liyue Harbor. Could you tell me more about the city?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: I'd like to hear about it too! I've never been!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon would like to start from Wanmin Restaurant...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How about I handle the explanations this time?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure, but don't you dare skip over any of the eating bits!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text:
"It is a port city built nestled against the mountains..."
You begin, only for Fujin to interrupt you. She notes that she'd like to hear "your" Liyue story.
You understand, and begin again.
"When we arrived in Liyue Harbor, Paimon and I were just in time for the Rite of Descension..."

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The child and adeptus before you listen to your words (and Paimon's incessant interjections), leaning forward as you speak, exclaiming in shock and relaxing as the tension in the tale rises and falls.\nThey also add their own commentary and questions about Liyue (such as the food and flavors available at restaurants, the toys the old lady sells, the gems and jewelry of Feiyun Slope, and such.)

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: As you watch Fujin, Little Mao, and Paimon be so moved by the tale...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Along this journey...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (We met many friends.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (We met many friends.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (And experienced so many things)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (And experienced so many things)

choices.text: (It was all worth it.)

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Wow! A sea monster, huh? Amazing!

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Liyue Harbor is... not what I imagined.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do you find it disappointing?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Well, no, just different, being different doesn't make it bad. I like the Liyue Harbor you described.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...It's good to hear that after all this time, our dear Herblord was able to find a home there. I think that's simply wonderful.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: What about you, Little Mao? Could you tell me about you and your friend? I'm curious to know what she's like.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: #Um, sure. I mean, Paimon and {NICKNAME} have met her already, so it wouldn't be fair if I didn't tell you.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: So, this is how we met...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: At that time, I was still a little kid who didn't know anything about the mountains. It was nighttime, and some wild beasts were following me through the forest. It was super scary!\nFinally, I was chased to a clearing, and surrounded by those beasties. For a moment, I was convinced I was gonna get eaten, but suddenly, they all backed off into the woods, and then they were gone.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: When I looked back, there she was, looking at me. She was like jade, but there was a dignity to her.\nI knew it then, that she was the master of the mountain that my grandparents had told me about. I wasn't scared. I just told her...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: "I finally found you! I've been looking for you for so long!"

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: I don't know why, but she lowered her head in thought before walking off. She made no noise as she did so. I listened as hard as I could, but there were no sounds of anything stepping on branches or fallen leaves.\nAfter that, I would sometimes catch sight of her, moving between trees in a flash. Sometimes, the rising moonlight would outline her shadow as she stood atop a high mountain.\nAt that time, I thought it was strange. Why hadn't I seen her before? She was always there, after all.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: I wanted to talk to her, but she would always turn and leave. It was only later that she became willing to talk to me. Much later on, she would take me up very high mountains and into very deep forests. She asked me a lot of questions, and in exchange, she told me lots of stories.\nIn the beginning, Qiaoying Village was a nameless, barren mountain, and the rivers had a real temper. Sometimes, they'd flood, and other times, they would all but wither.\nAnd on that barren mountain, she made two friends: a fish, and a snake...

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: But later, the snake was cut into pieces, and the fish sank into the sea... and then, only Bluey was left.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Thank you, Little Mao.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Also, um... Don't tell anyone about my friend, alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course we won't!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You seem quite familiar with this friend of Little Mao's, Fujin.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Indeed. But that was all in my past life. Many, many years have passed since I could no longer move freely. I suspect that I might not recognize her any longer, though from Little Mao's words, she might not have changed too much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Past life?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Hehe, perhaps that is not the most accurate way to phrase it. I did not utterly perish, but I did lose my original form, and my strength and wisdom dissipated along the spirit veins.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #This is also why I invited you and {NICKNAME} to Carp's Rest. If we were not there, I would not even have a form to show you or a voice with which to speak to you.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: It is thanks to you that I've been able to slowly regain my previous strength. Coming here and once more seeing these scenes with my own eyes, meeting old friends from the past... and more importantly, making new friends.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: I'm very glad.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How did you die?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...My memories of that have grown foggy. The Herblord and I were both servants of another god, and it was I that organized the Rainjade Rite, administering the rivers and mountains for our lord. As for the other... She was as she is — a beast, wild and free.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: In those peaceful days, I also climbed waterfalls to Mt. Aocang and Mt. Hulao, and there I met with the adepti, whose powers and wisdom far eclipse mine. Of course, that was all before the war.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Our lord was not a heinous being by any means. Once upon a time, she made many dreams come true — if there was any evil, it was the Archon War itself. What happened next needs no further explanation on my part, I'm sure.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You talked about how you and Herblord defected...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Hehe, that's right. That might've been the bravest thing we've ever done!

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Our lord had all but gone mad seeking the position of a god who may rule this world... or perhaps seeking survival. Either way, she lacked the power to overcome Morax.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: So, in a final, desperate gamble, she caused the Bishui River to flood, hoping to destroy everything downstream. Of course, she knew what that would mean for Chenyu Vale and its people.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa... But, uh, Paimon thinks that that's something you should never ever do, period...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Perhaps that's just what war does to people. Either way, that was our final adventure as a trio of friends.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Lingyuan attacked people with her familiars, herding them to the shelter we had prepared. Herblord fought against our mistress, while I climbed Mt. Lingmeng, and hurled the Votive Rainjade into the rising waters.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Of course, that wasn't a proper Rainjade Rite. It was simply the release of the adeptal energies stored within the jade pendant to have the earth open its maw and swallow the rivers, and allow the Jademouth to grow and stabilize the flow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, what happened next?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Hehe, didn't Little Mao tell you how it all ended?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Yeah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right... Wait. Really? When?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Alright, that's enough about the past. We should get back to performing the Rite itself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True... But what about the Golden Carp? Isn't that what we're looking for?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: In truth, you've already found it, as with the previous one. That's how I was able to appear before you.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: It's just that I missed the scenery here a bit too much, so I couldn't help but have a long chat with you all. After all, your sense of time and mine are not the same. You won't tarry long once your objectives are complete, will you?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: As such, I apologize. Please forgive my capriciousness.

choices.text: (I can only hope that in the end, it will all be worth it.)
Not sure why, but it reminds me of Madame Ping's...
Looks like it wasn't some sort of meaningless tradition after all.

talks.objective: Go back to look for Fujin

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Though my power is still a far cry from how it was in the past, thanks to your aid, I have regained much strength. Thank you. Next, we need to perform the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What effects will it have?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: It's been thousands of years since we last performed it, and the mountains, rivers, and spirit veins have all changed a great deal. But if all goes well, the Votive Rainjade will resolve the issue.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Well then, let's begin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The fog's dissipating...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa? What's that!?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Huh. It's just like in the mural! Do you remember, Paimon? The one with the two golden people, and something in between them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you're really impressive, Little Mao. Paimon didn't remember that at all!

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Behold, the sacred mountain.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: In my era, to merely climb it was already to transgress. But the ancestral inhabitants of this place are gone, and the communing path lies waste and broken. Who shall judge us now?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: That is where the spirit veins of Chenyu Vale converge. Through it, I can transmit my adeptal energy throughout the vale, restoring its water and its soil...

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: #We are only one step off from achieving our goal. Are you prepared, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's do this.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Indeed.

talks.objective: Take care of the nearby miasma

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Lingyuan... I perceived it would be you. And I do miss you so, but this really... might be a bad time.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Eh? So Bluey's name is Lingyuan?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Don't be like that. Speak with me.

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: The opportunity to speak will come, but it is not now. You know this.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: I know this, but I cannot allow it.

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Wait just a while longer. It will end soon.

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: I do not like the things up there. But it does not matter. Just leave it to me, Fujin.

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Do not come up here.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: I am quite sorry for not being completely frank with you earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Though I became aware of it during our travels, I did not wish to believe that my old friend Lingyuan would be the source of the storm that buffets Chenyu Vale.

choices.text: I actually had an inkling already...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? You did? When? How did you figure it out?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: She, Herblord, and I once defended Chenyu Vale together. To think that she would do something so wicked... Her disruption of the spirit veins has caused the miasma to propagate, and the one who stopped me from performing the Rite the first time was also her.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: But Big Sis Fujin... Bluey... I mean, Lingyuan, isn't a bad person...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...I know, Little Mao. She is your friend. But at this time, she is the greatest threat to Chenyu Vale. If she controls this sacred mountain, she will wield the power to completely alter the land of Chenyu Vale in the blink of an eye.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: I fear that Lingyuan has already entered Chiwang Terrace before us. She means to rewrite the flow and path of the spirit veins... We have little time left.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #{NICKNAME}. You have mastered the adeptal energy available here in Chenyu Vale. Lingyuan and her familiars will not be your match.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Please accompany me for a time and aid me, for the sake of the people in Chenyu Vale. I will perform a ritual and open up the way to Chiwang Terrace. Please stay by my side and... protect me.

choices.text: Whoa, so that's what's going on!

talks.objective: Take care of the nearby miasma

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Why won't you listen to me? Will you not wait?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Your strength is feeble. You cannot match me. But do not worry. You will soon recover.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: #Lingyuan... Say no more. {NICKNAME} and I will stop you. We will stop this... plan to destroy Chenyu Vale.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: The ritual is complete. The gate to Chiwang Terrace is now open!

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Lingyuan...

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Human. Let me tell you what you shall do. Fire arrows at my heart. If you approach up close, strike me with your sword. I will fight you to the last.

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: You are the only one here who can fight. When I have crushed your neck, I will triumph.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: No!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't intend to kill you.

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: ...Why? I do not understand.

choices.text: You've already lost.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: ...Fine. You may ask me one question.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You still really care about doing things like that, even though you lost, huh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then let us exchange questions.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Little Mao, do you have any questions?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Um... Bluey... Why did you have to fight? Can't we all be friends?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: You bunch of two-legged... And you, Fujin. You have not the strength to form two legs of your own, yet you wish to walk in their form and speak to me. But how can humans and wild beasts ever be friends?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: That's not true, Bluey, you're lying! If that's the case, why didn't you just let those beasts eat me back then? If humans and beasts can't be friends, and you're a beast, you shouldn't have helped me!

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: ...My actions are sometimes beyond even my own understanding. You were merely fortunate.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Well, why didn't you just eat Mountain as well? She almost bumped into you while lost in the fog at the foot of the mountain. I saw it!

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: You humans possess such wisdom that even nature submits to your will. In that case, you tell me. Why didn't I eat her?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? What kind of question is that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Mt. Laixin is dear to Adeptus Fujin.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: ...Let us just assume you are correct. She has told me much about the Rainjade Rite. Perhaps those memories affected my actions.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: You actually remembered everything I told you...

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Every year before the rite, you would tell me and that white snake how expectant you were, and how nervous. And after the rite, you would tell us how the festivities were so fun and lively. You would always speak, and I could not help but listen.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Only humans forget. I forget nothing.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: You have cleared this doubt of mine. Now, you may ask a question.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, Adeptus Fujin, have you any questions?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #Thank you, {NICKNAME}. Just a while back, Lingyuan, I was telling them stories about our past... Why do you wish to wreck Chenyu Vale, which we once fought so hard to protect?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: ...You planted tea trees, promising to enjoy tea with us. This too I remember. But that sort of tea no longer exists.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I want to change this land. I want to make it like it was all those millennia ago. You have walked with humans for too long. You have forgotten that you, I, and the snake all came from nature.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I knew that you never truly perished. And you did not depart this place like the snake. So I wish to change this place to the form it had when you were born. All these years, I have been slowly adjusting the spirit veins.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Oh, I get it! So that's where the miasma came from...

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Correct. Side effects. In the end, the process will change the soil, the waters, and the forests to what they should have been.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: What the soil, waters, and forest... should have been?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: You truly have forgotten the past. The rivers rose and fell with the rains, and their path was not fixed. The tea trees and flowers were not trimmed or cultivated, nor did they exist for humanity.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: In such an environment, you would regain your old form, and frolic once more in the great rivers. You would regain your strength. Spiritual power blanketed the land in those days, the wild shrubs grew thick. Now, the mountains and forests are silent, and the shimmering voice of the spring waters, tinkling like jade, can be heard no longer.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: But you don't understand. You still think you must stop me.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...Lingyuan, I count myself more blessed than most to have lived such a happy life, and in the end, my soul returned to my home. You are the one who does not understand.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Yes. And I have never understood. After you defeated me, you should have taken my territory. You planted tea on my mountain and gave that land to the humans. I do not understand why you did this.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Chenyu Vale was once but a nameless land, and we were nameless insects, beasts, and fish. I was the master of an uncultivated mountain, and today, that place belongs to neither of us.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: You took a human form and walked among them. You instituted the Rainjade Rite, and helped them change the soil and water. I did not understand then either, but I could see how happy you were.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: The snake changed into a human form and used her knowledge to create medicines and save the sick. I could understand how the agile human fingers could help her do what she wished, but I do not know why it was done.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: What happened after caused me still more confusion. You fought alongside humans and their so-called gods, and you perished. Humans fighting each other over territory and survival... Now that, I can understand.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: You both belong to the great river and the mountainous forests. You could have chosen to leave them and live on with me. Let that which is human belong to them, and nature belong to nature. Even if our territory were to shrink, we could still live freely.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: But now you wish to stop me and defend this land subdued by humanity. Answer me. Why?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Lingyuan, my friend... It is as you say. I do wish to protect them.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: ...Do not answer me with my own question! I was asking you why.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (This Lingyuan might be a beast, but she sure cares about the order of things, huh?)

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: (I know! That's how I learned so much from her.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...So you guys were just discussing stuff... in the mountains...?)

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: (Well, not totally. That said, after hearing everything Bluey said about Big Sis Fujin, I thought they'd be happy to meet each other...)

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: At first, I was like you. I did not understand humanity, and I did not enjoy their... excessive demands and love of hoarding, or their eternal desire to have more than they need, while caring so little for the needy themselves...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: "Trading," "wealth"... Like you, I did not understand these concepts and did not understand why they influence human joy and sorrow.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: But across the long years, I have also seen many other things.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: The cries of children break my heart, and the sound of an old person's shattered memories saddens me... Just as though it were all a microcosm of these mountains and rivers.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Have you noticed them, seen them? The children who wash their little feet in the streams, fishermen laughing beneath the light of the rainbow's arc, the moonlight trysts of lovebirds, their figures painted silver...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Humans, too, are creatures of this land. Just how different is their innocence from ours?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: ...You mean to say that you have chosen to take their side due to these emotions. Not through natural principles or logic. And not due to anyone's orders.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: I suspect that Herblord had much the same reasons as I. That said, I'm sure she'd put it all very differently, ha!

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I remain unsatisfied with your answer, Fujin. I do not understand.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Do you not? I think you've understood for a long time. When our lord... When our previous god raised the waters, it was you who brought your familiars around to attack the people and drive them to the shelters we had created.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I just...!

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: ...I just wished to help my friends. To make their wishes reality.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Even if doing so means going against nature and the principles you follow?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Even if it meant going against nature and the principles I follow, I would do so anyway.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Well, then we aren't all that different now, are we? Didn't you also choose your own position on account of your feelings?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I am satisfied with your answer, Fujin. Now, you may ask a question.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #Very well. May I ask the next question, {NICKNAME}, Paimon?

choices.text: Ask away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Paimon can't really think of any good questions at the moment. Since you've got one, you go right ahead!

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: You acknowledged my answer, acknowledged me, and acknowledged that you made choices based on your own feelings. Now, let me ask you...

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: N—No... Don't ask.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: You know what I'm going to ask you, right?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: "...If I needed your help, would you still make the same choice?"

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: That's right. And what's your answer?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: *sigh*...

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Yes. I would. Even should another thousand years pass, and even if you asked me a thousand more times, my answer would be the same.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: In that case, Lingyuan, I do in fact need your help. I truly wish to save the people of Chenyu Vale, so please, don't stop me from nursing the water and soil, alright?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: ...I promise you, Fujin. You have walked with humans for much time, and have learned their cunning, while I am but a foolish beast. My claws and teeth are sharp, but I am no match for you.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Thank you, Lingyuan.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #And thank you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and Little Mao. You've accompanied me for so long, and you've helped me a lot. I wouldn't have made it here without you.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe... I'm happy to have helped you, Big Sis! I'm so glad that Bluey got to meet you all, too. I was so worried when you fought...

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: #You also have my thanks, {NICKNAME}, Little Mao. It was you who brought Fujin to me. Though the circumstances of the meeting were not what I hoped for.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And what about Paimon?

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Alright, then. Let us begin.

choices.text: Eh? What about my question?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, why are you acting like a kid all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Yeah, that's really uncool of you!

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: #Ah, I apologize... But the question I wish to ask is very important, so I hope you can let me ask it. I'll make it up to you later, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: Eh, wasn't it Paimon's turn?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't really think of any good questions at the moment, so, uh... Since you wanna ask a question, Adeptus Fujin, go right ahead!

choices.text: You're Fujin's friend.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Big Sis Fujin? Big Sis...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where did she go?

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: Do you still not understand? She used all the energy she accumulated recently to nurse the land.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, if that's the case... Does that mean...

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: ...Yes. It is as you suspect.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... She struggled so hard to...

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Though we have now finished nursing the soil and water, the miasma that remains will not disappear immediately, so you'll have to be careful out there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Sorry for making you all see me like this. It is just as Lingyuan said. I have completely used up the energy I accumulated recently, and I can no longer maintain my favored form.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waaaaa... Paimon thought... Paimon thought that...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* Nothing, nothing! Paimon's glad you're still here, Adeptus Fujin! Seriously, Lingyuan...

dialogues.speaker: Lingyuan
dialogues.text: What about me?

choices.text: She wasn't entirely wrong, Paimon...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Though my form is as it has become, I am far more comfortable than before. At first, I was trapped at Carp's Rest, and could only reminisce about the outside world through the scent of the tea offerings.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: If I had not met you and Paimon, people of such compatibility with the spirit veins, I would have had none but my shadow to talk to, much less be able to leave Carp's Rest.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Thank you for your concern. Please forgive me, but I must depart now. I'll need a bit of rest.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: And another thing, Lingyuan.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Speak. What else would you have me do? Or not do.

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: Nothing. I just didn't get to say this due to the circumstances that prevailed before, but...

response.speaker: Fujin
response.text: ...But it's so good to see you again.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I know.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Thank you all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Where did that one come from...

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I should thank you for bringing her back. Safe, smooth, and slippery. Even the way in which her fins move is the same as I remember.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You sure have a, uh, strange way of remembering people... or fish, whichever.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I do not know how you did it, nor why you were able to obtain her adeptal energy. All these thousands of years, and I never once heard her voice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It might be due to {NICKNAME}'s, uh, unique constitution?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I see. However, I am but a foolish beast. Even if I wanted to see her again, I would not know of a better way.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I could only spend thousands of years clumsily imitating her methods, regulating the spirit veins in this land.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I am quite stupid, and I only knew this method, and so I did it — it was akin to scooping every droplet from a rushing river, or every grain of sand from the vast desert.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I knew as well that she would not smile as she once did, even if these mountains returned to how they once were.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: She, I, and the snake once laughed and swam happily here. Those days will never come again.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: She loves humanity too much, even more than she loves herself. Had I succeeded, she would only hate me.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: But that would have not mattered to me, so long as she could regain her form and swim free once more.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* And Paimon thought you were more concerned about nature...

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Of course I care. A land untamed by humans, a land of wild beasts. But that is a different subject from the matter of Fujin.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: If she thinks that a land tamed by humans is better, and that the strange tea leaves grown on such land taste superior, then I shall do what pleases her.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: So, thank you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Um, you're welcome?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, speaking of that, Paimon's curious. What did the tea leaves taste like in the past?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: When the land changed before, the tea leaves' flavor was much closer to what it was in the past, apart from some differences due to human influence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so you mean that the weirdly flavored teacakes we had were...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: In that case, I prefer the current flavor profile...

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Tea leaves cultivated by humanity will be more to their liking, of course. What I do not understand is Fujin's tastes.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: If the snake was here, we could ask for her opinion. But perhaps her tastes have also become strange from spending so much time with humans.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: #Before you go, {NICKNAME}, I have one final question for you.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Those that come from nature will, for some reason, go against nature — against the laws nature originally followed.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Will humans also go against humanity, against the principles they initially followed, for certain reasons?

choices.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Thank you. I have received the answer I desired.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: #Well then, Little Mao, {NICKNAME}, and Paimon. We shall meet again.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Alright then. See you later, Bluey!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Also, remember to take care of Big Sis Fujin! She seems kinda weak right now, so she could use some extra care!

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: I will. Farewell.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Please wait, Lingyuan.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have a question for you as well.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: Ask, then. I do owe you that.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If human activities are part of the laws of nature...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How would you view humanity?

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: A strange question. In the distant past, they were indeed part of nature. But they are so no longer. That is because...

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: No, I need to give this question more thought. Next time we meet, I will give you my answer.

choices.text: No.
That depends on the circumstances.

response.speaker: Lingyuan
response.text: You may as well have said just "yes."

choices.text: As long as you're still here, Adeptus Fujin.

talks.objective: Escort Little Mao back to Qiaoying Village

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Luo
dialogues.text: You're back! We were just saying that good rainfall's bound to bring good tidings! And what do you know, dear guests? You've arrived, right on time!

dialogues.speaker: Grandpa Lu
dialogues.text: How did it go? Well, I trust? Tell us all about it!

choices.text: It was thanks to Adeptus Fujin...

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: #So you met the legendary Carp Adeptus!? Oh my, as one would expect of the {M#young master}{F#young miss} of the Feiyun Commerce Guild. You really do have friends in high places!

choices.text: Hehe, it was a piece of cake for me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Anyway, your soil and water problems should be solved now!

response.speaker: Grandpa Lu
response.text: Haha, Old Luo, just what did I say? I told you it was a problem with the soil, but you wouldn't listen! If it wasn't for their help, we'd still be tealess come next year's Lantern Rite!

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: *cough* That, uh... Regardless, thank you both for your help, honored guests!

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: With your help, and the protection of the Carp Adeptus, I'm sure our village will surely see a great harvest of tea leaves this coming year.

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: Ah, yes, please take these. Take it as a token of our thanks!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Right, Paimon almost forgot! We came across this kid during our adventures. Is he from the village, too?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe, Uncle Luo, I'm back!

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: Well, if it isn't you, Little Mao? Finally of a mind to come back, huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? You don't seem worried at all...

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: And what is there to fret about? This kid runs around in the mountains all the time, and he always comes back safe after getting tired. If you ask me, there's been an adeptus looking after him in secret all along! You know, maybe that might even have been said Carp Adeptus...

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: I've said it before — that wasn't an adeptus. It was Bluey—

response.speaker: Grandpa Lu
response.text: Alright, alright, Little Mao, don't argue with Luo here. He's just pretending to know what he's talking about. Come by my place later — I'll make you some egg custard!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Woohoo! Egg custard!

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: Hmph, and now you pretend to be a good person... Wait, what do you mean, "pretending to know"?

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: ...In any case, I don't really know how to repay you, dear guests.

response.speaker: Uncle Luo
response.text: If you should need any help in the future, Qiaoying Village will be there to lend you a hand!

choices.text: Now, your water and soil problems should be no more.
We were able to clear the source of the anomalies...

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: #You're awesome, {NICKNAME}! You pushed the moss back just like that — like you did with that smoky cloud!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Still, that wasn't there yesterday. Is this what they call "nature"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Don't worry about it. Moss or hilichurls, just leave 'em all to {NICKNAME}! Little Mao, what's this picture about?

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Hehehe! Originally, I didn't know either, but I figured it out today after hearing Big Sis Fujin's story! This must be the stuff that happened before the mural on Mt. Lingmeng was made!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: See this? Long, long ago, people were able to talk to the gods and adepti in the skies by talking to that big piece of jade in the middle.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: The emissary of the gods would lead them and protect them. See, that's gotta be this shiny golden person standing in the middle — I bet that was a super amazing person.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: But later, just like Big Sis Fujin said, something changed, and the people of Chenyu Vale lost their guiding emissary, and they couldn't talk to the heavens any longer — that's how the Rainjade Rite came about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Your story does make sense!

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: #Hehe, thanks! What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: You're a pretty bright spark, Little Mao.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe...

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Come to think of it, our ancestors were pretty amazing themselves, huh? The jades they left to us still have the power to restore nature! For something this old to still be so strong, the past must've been a sweller time than the present, huh?

choices.text: That's not true. The world marches onward.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Leaving the accumulated detritus of the past in its wake.

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Huh... That's a really cool thought. I never thought about it that way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon thinks that you're the amazing one, Little Mao. We've seen lots of ancient objects, puzzles, mysterious powers, and monsters in our time, but Paimon's never considered this stuff before...

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Hehe. Oh, you know what? Not thinking about this stuff at all is pretty awesome too, really! I bet you'll be just like my big sister when you grow up, just having fun adventuring everywhere!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, you have a big sister, then?

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: Well, we're not blood-related, but she worked here in Chenyu Vale for a while. She'd go up mountains and run around the rivers, and I'd follow her! We discovered this little cave together!

response.speaker: Little Mao
response.text: She said that this cave is my "Rubicon"... Not that I know what that means...

choices.text: That's right. The world's been constantly in decline.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...But even so, we shouldn't give up on the future.

choices.text: That's a distinct possibility.
I'm not sure.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: The Sacred Simulacra... During the earliest festivals, people didn't know how they should carve the statues, and the products turned out a real mess. Even that friend of mine couldn't help but burst into laughter upon seeing it...

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: #Ah... Sorry about that, {NICKNAME}, I got lost in the past again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why did Little Mao disappear while we weren't looking?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did he run up ahead of us? There's lots of monsters around here. Let's go up ahead and look.

dialogues.speaker: Little Mao
dialogues.text: Well, that's Mt. Xuanlian right up ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice. Let's see what clues we can find.

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Please, come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Fujin? Wait, why'd you turn into a Golden Carp again?

dialogues.speaker: Fujin
dialogues.text: Well, this form makes movement easier. Do you not like it, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, no. Paimon's just not used to talking to a fish.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The world seems to spin for a moment, and when you open your eyes once more, you are already above the clouds...
